record.context_brief: Phase transitions for torus distance energy
record.original_question: Let Ω=T^2 be the flat torus with distance ρ(x,y)=min_{k∈Z^2} ‖x−y+k‖, and for α>0 consider the energy I_α(μ)=∫∫ρ(x,y)^α dμ(x)dμ(y). Since the uniform measure σ maximizes I_α at α=1 while measures of the form (δ_p+δ_{p*})/2 maximize it at α=2, what are the phase transition point or points between these maximizing regimes?

evidence.quote: Problem 4.2 (Dmitriy Bilyk). Let Ω = T2 be the flat torus with ρ(x, y) = min k∈Z2 ∥x − y + k∥. What are the phase transition points in this case?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega = \mathbb{T}^2 = \mathbb{R}^2/\mathbb{Z}^2$ be the flat 2-torus, equipped with the quotient distance
$$\rho(x,y) = \min_{k\in\mathbb{Z}^2} \|x-y+k\|,$$
where $\|\cdot\|$ denotes the Euclidean norm on $\mathbb{R}^2$. For a parameter $\alpha>0$ and a Borel probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{T}^2$, define the distance energy
$$I_\alpha(\mu) = \iint_{\mathbb{T}^2\times\mathbb{T}^2} \rho(x,y)^\alpha \, d\mu(x)\,d\mu(y).$$
It is known that:
(i) at $\alpha=1$, the normalized uniform (Lebesgue) measure $\sigma$ on $\mathbb{T}^2$ maximizes $I_\alpha$ among all Borel probability measures on $\mathbb{T}^2$;
(ii) at $\alpha=2$, the maximizers are the two-point measures of the form $\tfrac{1}{2}(\delta_p + \delta_{p^*})$, where $p^* = p + (\tfrac{1}{2},\tfrac{1}{2}) \pmod{\mathbb{Z}^2}$ is the antipode of $p$ in $\mathbb{T}^2$.

Determine the set of phase transition points: i.e., find the value(s) $\alpha^*\in(1,2)$ at which the family of maximizers of $I_\alpha$ on $\mathbb{T}^2$ changes type, and describe the maximizing measure(s) on each subinterval of $(0,\infty)$ delimited by these transition values.
artifact.category_tag: Distance energy optimization on the torus
artifact.status_search_result: No published resolution was located. Recent work by Bilyk and collaborators on geodesic distance Riesz energies on related manifolds (e.g., projective spaces) explicitly describes the existence and structure of phase transitions as an active area, and the analogous question on the flat torus appears not to have been settled in the literature found.

status_evidence.title: Geodesic Distance Riesz Energy on Projective Spaces
status_evidence.snippet: minimizers of this energy undergo numerous phase transitions, in sharp contrast with many analogous known examples (even the seemingly similar geodesic Riesz energy on the sphere), which usually have only one transition (between uniform and discrete minimizers)
status_evidence.claim: Phase transitions for distance-type energies are an active topic; the torus case is not resolved in this work.

status_evidence.title: Stolarsky principle and energy optimization on the sphere
status_evidence.snippet: Energy optimization for distance-type kernels on spheres, with phase transitions between uniform and discrete maximizers.
status_evidence.claim: Related sphere results exist but the torus phase transition problem is not addressed.
